title: An exactly solvable macroscopic fluctuation theory of single-file diffusion
authors: Sandeep Jangid, Soumyabrata Saha, Kapil Sharma, Jitendra Kethepalli, Benjamin Guiselin, Jacopo De Nardis, Tridib Sadhu
abstract: Single-file diffusion is a ubiquitous phenomenon in low-dimensional systems, arising in transport inside narrow channels. Its natural continuum model is a one-dimensional gas of extended Brownian hard rods (BHR). Perhaps owing to the perceived intractability of this problem, much of the literature has traditionally focused on lattice exclusion models, where integrability methods have yielded remarkable, albeit limited, exact results. A major recent advance comes from a formal solution of macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) for the exclusion process. Yet, despite the formal solution, only a handful of properties have been made explicit. We show that the corresponding MFT of the extended BHR gas is in fact exactly solvable through a canonical transformation. We demonstrate this by explicit computation of the large-deviation statistics of the tracer-position and integrated-current in both annealed and quenched ensembles. We further show that an analogous canonical transformation applies to the MFT of lattice gases with finite-volume exclusion, yielding corresponding tracer and current statistics. We validate our results using rare-event simulations for both the continuum and the lattice models.
summary: This paper provides an exact solution to the macroscopic fluctuation theory governing single-file diffusion using the Brownian Hard Rod model. The authors achieve this by applying a canonical transformation that maps the complex interacting system onto a solvable point-particle description. This yields explicit, universal large-deviation statistics for observables like tracer position and integrated current in both annealed and quenched environments.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an exactly solvable macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) for single-file diffusion, a process common in low-dimensional systems.
main_result: They show that the MFT for the extended Brownian Hard Rod gas is exactly solvable via a canonical transformation, yielding explicit large-deviation statistics for key observables.
method: The core method involves mapping the fluctuating hydrodynamic equation governing the density field onto an exactly solvable point-particle system using a canonical transformation. Large deviation functions and scaled cumulant generating functions are calculated in both annealed and quenched ensembles.
model_or_system: The primary model is single-file diffusion, modeled by a one-dimensional gas of extended Brownian Hard Rods (BHR). The theory is generalized to lattice gases with finite-volume exclusion.
key_observables: Tracer-position ($z_t$), integrated-current ($Q_t$), and the local-height observable $h(z)_t$.
important_parameters: Hard rod length ($a$), bare diffusion coefficient ($D_0=1$), time scaling ($\sqrt{t}$), and ensemble type (annealed vs. quenched).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-time asymptotic behavior of fluctuations, characterized by saddle-point approximations in the path integral formalism.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate BHR trajectories, show LDFs for tracer-position and integrated-current comparing theory to simulation, and display optimal density profile evolution associated with specific SCGF variables.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the continuum model (BHR) and its hydrodynamic description. It then introduces the canonical transformation that renders the MFT solvable. Finally, it derives explicit formulas for the SCGFs of tracer-position and integrated-current, comparing results across different ensembles and showing connections to local-height statistics.
why_interesting: The techniques used—mapping complex interacting systems (like BHR) onto exactly solvable point-particle models via canonical transformations—are highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems where exact solutions are rare.
